text: I'll start with the deployment named in the page.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment orders/orders-api was released with its readiness probe pointed at the wrong port. The container listens on 8080 (its own log says "orders-api: serving on :8080", and the container port declared in the template is 8080), but .spec.template.spec.containers[api].readinessProbe.httpGet.port is 8081. Nothing is bound to 8081 in the pod, so every readiness probe gets "connect: connection refused" and both pods stay Ready=False. Because Endpoints only publish ready pods, Service orders/orders-api holds both pod IPs under notReadyAddresses and has zero endpoint addresses, so checkout-gateway's calls to the orders backend have nowhere to land ("gateway: orders fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)"), which surfaces as 5xx at the checkout gateway. Fix: set the readiness probe port to 8080 in the Deployment template.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment orders/orders-api sets .spec.template.spec.containers[api].readinessProbe.httpGet.port to 8081 while the api container listens on 8080 ("orders-api: serving on :8080", containerPort 8080), so the kubelet's readiness HTTP GET is refused — 'Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.0.122:8081/": dial tcp 10.244.0.122:8081: connect: connection refused' — and the kubelet keeps both pods marked Ready=False (deployment ready=0/2) as the probe repeats every 5s.

evidence.claim: Both orders-api pods run but are not ready and the Service has no endpoint addresses.
Service orders-api has zero endpoint addresses.
The Deployment's readiness probe targets port 8081 while the declared container port is 8080.
The probe is refused at 8081 on the pod IP.
evidence.quote: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.0.122:8081/": dial tcp 10.244.0.122:8081: connect: connection refused

evidence.claim: Both pod IPs are held as notReadyAddresses, so no traffic is routed to them.
The gateway's calls to the orders backend do not complete.
evidence.quote: gateway: orders fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)

ruled_out.alternative: Service selector does not match the pod labels
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service selector app=orders-api matches the pod labels exactly; the endpoint controller does select both pods, it just lists them as not ready.

ruled_out.alternative: Service targetPort points at the wrong container port
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Service orders-api targets port 8080, which is the port the container actually serves on, so the Service port mapping is correct.

ruled_out.alternative: The application is crashing or failing to start (bad image, missing configmap volume)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The container started, has zero restarts and is Running with its script volume mounted; only readiness is failing.
